claim: Let \(A_1A_2A_3A_4\) be a regular tetrahedron with circumcenter \(O\) and circumradius \(R>0\). For every point \(P\in\mathbb R^3\), put \(\rho=OP\) and \(\Pi(P)=\prod_{i=1}^4 PA_i\). At each fixed \(\rho\ge0\), the complete attainable interval is \[|R-\rho|\left(R^2+\rho^2+\frac{2R\rho}{3}\right)^{3/2}\le \Pi(P)\le (R+\rho)\left(R^2+\rho^2-\frac{2R\rho}{3}\right)^{3/2}.\] For \(\rho>0\), equality on the left occurs exactly on the four rays from \(O\) through the vertices, and equality on the right exactly on the four opposite rays; every intermediate value occurs.

scientific limitations/integrity.integrity: The infinite statement is proved analytically by a tight-frame reduction, Lagrange-multiplier classification of every stationary direction, exact factor comparisons, and connectedness of the direction sphere. The bundled finite checker is a reproducibility test only and is not used as a substitute for the proof. No independent audit has been performed.
scientific limitations/integrity.limitations: The theorem is restricted to Euclidean regular tetrahedra in dimension three. No higher-dimensional analogue is asserted. A 1995 one-page note on regular simplicial distances was not directly available in full text; an older equivalent extremal formulation under different terminology therefore remains a residual literature risk.

title: Sharp radial product profile for vertex distances in a regular tetrahedron
